name: BrowserStack
summary: BrowserStack runs a cloud testing platform that lets teams test websites and apps on real browsers and devices, and it describes itself as remote-first. Candidates commonly report coding and problem-solving rounds, a design or project deep dive for experienced engineers, and questions that reflect its published values, such as Think Big, Sense of Urgency and Solve Problems for Scale.
rounds: Online or live coding round for engineering roles (often)
System design or project deep dive for experienced roles
looks_for: Understanding of testing: automation, flaky tests, real devices and CI pipelines
Working well in a remote-first team

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to move fast on something urgent without cutting the corners that mattered.
covers: Why it was urgent and what waiting would have cost
What you skipped and what you refused to skip
The result, and any clean-up you did afterwards

questions.text: Describe something you built that kept working as usage grew, without a redesign.
covers: The early design choices that allowed it to grow
How usage grew and what you watched
What you would design differently with hindsight

questions.text: Tell me about a time you were wrong about something technical. How did you find out?
covers: What you believed and why it seemed right
The evidence or person that showed you otherwise
How you changed your view and what you learned

questions.text: Tell me about a time you put the team's goal ahead of your own work.
covers: The team goal and the conflict with your own task
What you did and how you communicated it
The outcome for the team and for your own work

questions.text: Describe a time a constraint pushed you to a better idea.
covers: The constraint: time, cost, hardware, a rule
The idea it forced, and why it was better
Proof it worked

questions.text: How would you design a service that gives a user a real mobile device in the cloud for a testing session?
covers: A device pool: allocation, queueing when busy and health checks
Streaming the screen and input with low delay
Wiping and resetting each device after a session, for privacy and reliability

questions.text: What makes automated UI tests flaky, and how would you reduce flakiness in a large test suite?
covers: Causes: timing and waits, shared test data, test order, unstable environments
Fixes: explicit waits, isolated data, retries only with tracking
Measuring flakiness per test and quarantining the worst offenders

questions.text: How would you run thousands of browser tests in parallel for one customer and report results quickly?
covers: Splitting the suite and scheduling it across many browser instances
Fair sharing between customers, and limits per plan
Collecting logs, screenshots and videos so failures are easy to debug

questions.text: A customer says their tests pass locally but fail on our platform. How would you investigate?
covers: Comparing environments: browser version, screen size, network, time zone
Using the session's logs and video to find the first difference
Fixing our side or guiding the customer, and documenting the cause

questions.text: Explain at a high level how a tool like Selenium or Playwright controls a browser.
covers: The test script sends commands through a driver or browser protocol
How elements are found and actions carried out
Why waits and synchronisation matter

questions.text: What's the difference between unit, integration and end-to-end tests, and how would you balance them for a web app?
covers: What each level checks and how fast and stable it is
Many fast unit tests, fewer integration tests, a small set of end-to-end flows
An example of a bug only one level would catch

questions.text: How would you help an enterprise customer's QA team move from mostly manual testing to automation?
covers: Understanding their app, team skills and release process first
Starting with a few high-value, stable flows and their CI pipeline
Showing progress: time saved, bugs caught earlier, release confidence

questions.text: Why BrowserStack? What appeals to you about building tools for developers and testers?
covers: Any real experience testing across browsers or devices
What you find interesting in the problem: scale, devices, developer experience
What you'd like to work on first

questions.text: BrowserStack is remote-first. How do you keep your work visible and stay connected with a team you rarely meet?
covers: Habits: written updates, clear handovers, asking for help early
How you handle time zones and overlapping hours
An example from remote or hybrid work

tips: If you can, try the product yourself: run a site on a few real browsers and devices so you can speak as a user.
Know the testing landscape: Selenium, Playwright, Cypress, Appium, CI pipelines and why tests become flaky.
Show a sense of urgency in your stories, but pair it with how you protected quality.
For remote-first work, give concrete habits rather than saying you're self-motivated.
